name: Non-Immigrant ED Visa (Education)
summary: The Non-Immigrant ED visa is for studying in Thailand: at a university, an international or Thai school, a licensed Thai language school or a Muay Thai school that is allowed to sponsor students. The school sponsors you, you enter for 90 days, and you extend in Thailand for as long as your course lasts. You have to study for real: attendance is checked.
seoTitle: Thailand ED Visa 2026: Study, Thai Language and Muay Thai
seoDescription: How the Thai Non-Immigrant ED student visa works for universities, Thai language schools and Muay Thai camps: fees, documents, extensions, and how it compares with the DTV.
validity: Single entry, valid 3 months from issue, with a stay of up to 90 days on arrival. Some embassies also issue a multiple-entry ED visa valid for 1 year.
extendableDetail: You extend at the immigration office with a letter from your school. For language schools, Muay Thai schools and other non-formal schools, each extension is up to 90 days and the total is normally capped at one year. University and formal school students can be extended for the period the institution certifies, up to one year at a time.
feeNote: Embassy pages list 2,000 THB for a single-entry ED visa (valid 3 months) and 5,000 THB for a multiple-entry visa (valid 1 year), charged in local currency and paid by card on the e-Visa system. Extensions in Thailand cost 1,900 THB each. School fees are separate and often the biggest cost.
financialRequirement: No single national figure. Embassies ask for bank statements showing you can pay tuition and living costs; for example, the Tokyo embassy asks for at least 30,000 THB, held for the past three months. Check the page of the embassy or e-Visa country you apply in.
processingTime: Processing times vary by embassy and are shown on each embassy's e-Visa page. Your school also needs time, often a couple of weeks, to get its paperwork from the Ministry of Education or other authority, so start early.
keyRequirements: Enrolment at an institution that is licensed and allowed to sponsor ED visas
A sponsorship letter from the school plus a letter from the relevant authority (Ministry of Education, or for Muay Thai the Sports Authority of Thailand or another relevant body)
A passport valid for at least 6 months
Proof of funds for tuition and living costs, as set by your embassy
Regular attendance: immigration checks your study when you extend
documents: Passport biodata page (at least 6 months' validity)
Recent passport photo (taken within the last 6 months)
Letter confirming enrolment, signed by an authorised person at the school, with a copy of their ID card or passport
Letter from the relevant authority: Ministry of Education (schools), the university itself (degree courses), or for Muay Thai training a body such as the Sports Authority of Thailand
Bank statements showing enough funds, usually for the past three months
Proof of your current address or legal residence in the country where you apply
For degree courses: your previous academic certificate
For monks, nuns and priests studying Dharma: a letter from the National Office of Buddhism

howToApply.step: Choose a school that can sponsor you
howToApply.detail: Ask the school directly whether it holds a current licence and can issue ED visa paperwork. Many gyms and language schools can't. Pay the course fee only once they confirm this in writing.
The school sends you an enrolment letter and the letter from the relevant authority. Check that the names, passport number and course dates match your passport exactly.

howToApply.step: Apply for the ED visa online
howToApply.detail: Apply on thaievisa.go.th (or at the embassy if your country isn't on the e-Visa system yet), upload your documents and pay by card. Print the approved e-Visa and bring it when you fly.

howToApply.step: Start classes and report your address
howToApply.detail: Your accommodation must file the TM30 address notification for you. Attend classes from the start: schools keep attendance records and may report to the authorities.

Take the school's extension letter, attendance record, passport, photo, TM7 form and the 1,900 THB fee to your local immigration office. Officers sometimes ask a few questions about your course, or a few words of Thai if you study the language.
Report your address every 90 days if you stay that long on one extension, and get a re-entry permit before you leave Thailand during your course.

bestFor: Students at Thai universities and international or Thai schools
People taking a structured Thai language course
Muay Thai students who want to train at one licensed camp with a fixed schedule
Interns and exchange students on a course-linked programme
notFor: Anyone who wants to work, including part-time or remote work
People who want to train at several different gyms or travel a lot (the DTV is more flexible)
Short training trips of a few weeks (the visa exemption may be enough)
Anyone using a school only as a paper route to stay in Thailand. Immigration actively checks and cancels these visas.
commonMistakes: Paying for a course before checking that the school can legally sponsor an ED visa.
Skipping classes. Poor attendance can lead to your extension being refused or your visa being cancelled.
Working, even online, on an ED visa.
Leaving Thailand without a re-entry permit, which cancels your extension.
Expecting unlimited extensions at a language or Muay Thai school. The total is normally one year.

faqs.q: Can I get an ED visa to train Muay Thai?
faqs.a: Yes, if the camp is set up to sponsor students. Muay Thai training is listed as an ED purpose by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, supported by a letter from a relevant body such as the Sports Authority of Thailand. Many gyms don't hold the right licence, so ask before you pay.

faqs.q: Muay Thai ED visa or DTV: which is better?
faqs.a: The ED visa ties you to one school: 90 days on entry, then 90-day extensions, usually up to a year, with attendance checked. The Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) is a 5-year multiple-entry visa with stays of up to 180 days, lets you train at any camp and allows remote work for foreign clients, but it needs 500,000 THB in savings and costs more. If you have the savings and want flexibility, the DTV usually fits better. If you're committing to one camp for a year and don't have the savings, the ED is the usual route.

faqs.q: Can I study Thai on the DTV instead?
faqs.a: Thai language schools are not on the list of approved Soft Power activities for the DTV. If your reason for coming is to study Thai, the ED visa is the right choice.

faqs.q: How long can I stay on a language school ED visa?
faqs.a: Up to 90 days per extension, with a total normally capped at one year from your entry. University and formal school students can stay for the length of their course, extended up to a year at a time.

faqs.q: Can I work part-time or online while on an ED visa?
faqs.a: No. The ED visa does not allow any work. If you want to work remotely for foreign clients while training, the DTV allows that.

Yes. Schools keep attendance records and immigration may ask about your course when you extend. Since 2025 the authorities have stepped up checks on ED visas used without genuine study, and visas have been cancelled.

faqs.q: Can I change to an ED visa inside Thailand?
faqs.a: Some immigration offices allow a change of visa type in Thailand if you entered on a visa exemption or tourist visa, but it's discretionary and rules differ by office. Applying from abroad through the e-Visa system is the safer route.
